TECHNOLOGY_DECISIONS.PURPOSE: Defines the transport, cryptographic format, server-side token storage, Android distribution, and endpoint-security technologies for the opaque realtime wake-event flow specified by RA36-001.
TECHNOLOGY_DECISIONS.DECISION: Require a separate -ntfy-origin runtime flag; do not reuse -public-origin. Accept only an HTTPS origin with a host and optional explicit port, with no userinfo, query or fragment and with only an empty or root path. Validate the configured origin at startup and fail closed on invalid or missing input. Validate every registered Endpoint independently against this origin.

Configure the outbound ntfy HTTP client with a request timeout of 5s by default and expose -ntfy-timeout as a runtime duration option. Reject zero or negative durations at startup. Propagate the worker/service context cancellation to each request, disable redirects, and treat every redirect as a terminal delivery failure without following it. Record UNKNOWN when timeout, cancellation or a transport error leaves acceptance ambiguous. Never roll back committed message state and do not automatically retry delivery in the first implementation.

Use self-hosted ntfy Server v2.34.0 as the sole realtime push server and ntfy Android v1.25.2 as the UnifiedPush distributor. The BFE Chat Android application integrates connector 3.3.5, receives the push in its own process, and creates the Android system notification.

Use the UnifiedPush registration endpoint with its p256dh public key and auth secret as the Web Push subscription. Encrypt payloads using RFC 8291 and the aes128gcm content encoding. The selected Go standard-library primitives are P-256 ECDH, HKDF-SHA256, and AES-GCM.

The encrypted application payload contains only protocol version and opaque wakeToken. Use generic notification text; keep wakeToken in the notification's internal navigation state, not in visible notification text or a URL.

Generate wakeToken with Go crypto/rand and persist its conversation mapping in PostgreSQL. Resolve tokens only through the protected Chat API; authorization and token-lifecycle behavior follow REQ36-WAKE-TOKEN and REQ32-AUTH.

Store the complete Endpoint URL returned by the ntfy Android v1.25.2 UnifiedPush registration, the public encryption key, and the authentication secret as protected subscription data associated with the authenticated BFE account. Endpoint is the sole delivery-destination field: do not accept or persist a separate Topic and do not derive a Topic from Endpoint. Preserve the complete Endpoint unchanged for delivery. Registration, replacement, and removal use the protected Chat API and session-bound DPoP. A subscription identifies a delivery destination and grants no conversation or history access. Endpoint URLs, registration secrets, wakeToken values, and full push payloads are not logged or returned to other accounts.

Treat the complete registered Endpoint as a bearer capability. Require HTTPS and exact origin equality with the configured ntfy origin. For the pinned ntfy Android v1.25.2 distributor, validate the returned URL format as one path segment matching /up followed by exactly 12 ASCII alphanumeric characters and the exact query up=1; reject userinfo, fragments, extra path segments, trailing slash, percent-encoded path variants, extra query parameters, malformed URLs and origin mismatch. The pinned ntfy v2.34.0 server accepts topic names from the ASCII topic character set and applies the UnifiedPush up-prefix and length-14 convention; the pinned Android distributor creates the 12-character alphanumeric suffix and returns the full URL with ?up=1. Reject arbitrary client-supplied hosts, redirects, invalid schemes and origins outside the configured server to prevent SSRF. Validate each Endpoint independently; do not split out, store or independently select a Topic. The Endpoint value cannot expand the configured destination origin.

Run ntfy v2.34.0 as a private self-hosted HTTPS instance with auth-default-access: deny-all. Follow the documented ntfy UnifiedPush distributor setup: the BFE Chat publisher uses anonymous write-only access to the up* topic pattern and has no ntfy account/admin credentials; the ntfy Android distributor uses a regular non-admin account with read-only access to the up* topic pattern. Never grant anonymous read or read-write access, and never grant anonymous access to all topics. Publish to the complete Endpoint URL returned by UnifiedPush registration, including its path and up=1 query; do not pass or persist a separate Topic. Encrypt each payload according to RFC 8291 for its registered endpoint; ntfy topic access does not replace Chat API authorization. Do not expose ntfy administrative credentials to BFE Chat or end-user clients.

The BFE Chat Android client posts a generic system notification. Its internal intent carries protocol version and wakeToken. Activation resolves the token through the protected Chat API before conversation navigation and authenticated history retrieval.

When Chat is administratively disabled, new Chat operations, history requests, wakeToken resolution, and new UnifiedPush registrations are denied. An already-active ntfy subscription may continue delivering only the opaque wake payload; receiving it does not authorize any API request. After re-enable, authorized clients catch up through the existing history API.

Persist a durable per-recipient delivery intent in the same PostgreSQL transaction as the message and idempotency result. After commit, a background worker processes the durable intents; the HTTP request path must not wait for outbound ntfy delivery, and no network I/O occurs inside the message transaction. A delivery failure never rolls back a committed message. Record a sanitized terminal outcome. A timeout, cancellation or transport failure whose acceptance status cannot be determined is UNKNOWN. The first implementation performs no automatic delivery retries, including for UNKNOWN; an interrupted claimed attempt is terminal UNKNOWN rather than re-dispatched. An idempotent message replay creates no new delivery intent. Missed notifications are recovered through authenticated history.

PostgreSQL 18.4 stores conversation data, authoritative message history, read state, and durable wakeToken mappings. pgx v5 provides PostgreSQL access and transaction support; Goose v3 manages schema migrations. BFE Drive Internal Auth over UDS validates session-bound DPoP. Realtime events are hints only; persisted conversation history remains authoritative for catch-up, ordering, visibility, and read state. No API versioning, legacy-data migration, or legacy-client support is introduced by these technology choices.

Pinned source confirms the returned Endpoint format /up followed by 12 ASCII alphanumeric characters and the exact query up=1.
